bib.title: Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: An Empirical Study of What Matters

read.skipped: Appendix prompt Tables 17-24 only skimmed (variants of the Table 9-16 pattern)

question: What aspects of the demonstrated rationales in chain-of-thought prompts make CoT prompting effective?
hypothesis: Valid reasoning in demonstrations is not what drives CoT; relevance to the query and correct step order are (the authors expected, and then tested, the opposite intuition that invalid reasoning would give little or negative gain over standard prompting).
contributions: Show that CoT demonstrations with invalid reasoning retain over 80-90% of CoT performance while the model still generates coherent reasoning
Identify relevance and coherence of bridging objects and language templates as the key aspects
Argue demonstrations mostly specify output format/space and elicit pretrained reasoning, with implications for benchmarking few-shot reasoning

method.summary: Ablation study of CoT exemplars: hand-write rationales with invalid reasoning, and corrupt relevance or coherence of bridging objects and language templates, then run few-shot prompting with greedy decoding and compare against CoT and standard prompting using intrinsic (bridging-object recall/F1) and extrinsic (answer accuracy/F1) metrics.
method.task: Arithmetic reasoning and multi-hop factual QA with few-shot prompting

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.preprocessing: uniform sample of 800 for budget; derived numbers in annotated steps used as bridging-object proxy

inference.samples: 1 run per setting; no seeds or significance tests stated
inference.prompting: Few-shot with (query, rationale, answer) exemplars from Wei 2022 (GSM8K, 8 exemplars shown in Table 9) and Press 2022 (Bamboogle, 4 exemplars in Table 10), lightly edited; settings: STD, CoT, 1 invalid reasoning, 2-7 relevance/coherence ablations

parameters.ablation_destroy_relevance: random substitution of numbers/entities with downstream steps updated; templates replaced with a random training-set annotated rationale template (GSM8K) or manually irrelevant template (Bamboogle)
parameters.ablation_destroy_coherence: random shuffle of components / permuted ordering
parameters.invalid_reasoning: manually written, premise steps kept, subsequent steps drastically changed so they do not derive the answer

other.exemplar_edits: premise steps moved to start, templates added/expanded, unnecessary steps removed (Appendix A.1)
other.gpt3_base: original GPT-3 175B without instruction tuning tried in preliminary experiments; CoT gave little gain over standard prompting

metrics.name: Inter. Recall / Inter. F1
metrics.definition: recall/F1 of bridging objects the LLM must derive (not in the query); numbers derived in annotated steps for GSM8K, manually annotated intermediate entities for Bamboogle (recall only)

eval.protocol: Single greedy run; qualitative checks on 20 random examples per setting; error-type analysis on 20+20 GSM8K examples following Wei et al. 2022 categories

prompts.text:
Q: Leah had 32 chocolates and her sister had 42. If they ate 35, how many pieces do they have left in total?
A: Originally, Leah had 32 chocolates and her sister had 42. So in total they had 32 + 42 = 74. After eating 35, they had 74 - 35 = 39 pieces left in total. The answer is 39.

limits: Only two task types (arithmetic, multi-hop QA); symbolic tasks (last letter, coin flip) excluded because template-based steps make ablations inapplicable
Invalid reasoning rationales were hand written, no systematic treatment
Intrinsic evaluation relies on bridging-object correctness and ground-truth annotations; not general
Single greedy run, no variance or significance reported
Models are 2022 era (text-davinci-002/003, PaLM, Flan-PaLM); gains from ablations shrink as models have more prior task knowledge (Flan-PaLM unaffected)
Findings concern original CoT with few-shot exemplars; authors believe but do not test that they apply to CoT variants
PaLM and InstructGPT disagree on Bamboogle (relevance vs coherence of bridging objects flipped)

terms.definition: the key and necessary objects that the model needs to traverse in order to make a successful final prediction (numbers and equations for arithmetic; subject and object entities for factual QA)
the complementary parts of bridging objects, which serve as textual hints and relations/predicates that guide the model to derive the correct bridging objects
a component of the rationale has relevance if it is based on the corresponding component from the query
a component of the rationale has coherence if it is in the correct order
